blocks.title: Communication needs an agreement about who drives what
paragraphs: I/O connects devices with different timing and service needs to the processor/memory system. A bus transaction needs an address or device selection, data direction and control/timing that tells participants when information is valid.
Polling asks software to check device status; interrupts let an event request attention. Neither mechanism removes the need to identify the device, transfer data and acknowledge completion correctly.

blocks.title: Separate selection, driving and completion
paragraphs: Only the selected driver should drive a shared data line during a transfer. A tri-state output can be high, low or high-impedance; high-impedance releases the line and is not another Boolean data value.

A synchronous interface uses its defined clock timing. An asynchronous handshake signals readiness/completion explicitly. In either case, hold information valid for the specified interval and avoid interpreting an undriven bus as valid data.

A daisy-chain grant passes priority through an ordered chain. Position affects which requester sees a grant first under that scheme; this is distinct from a separately specified programmable priority rule.

blocks.title: Ignored address lines produce aliases
paragraphs: Consider an eight-bit byte address with decoder lines A0 and A3 ignored. Address 0x24 has the same decoded bits as 0x25, 0x2C and 0x2D. Varying two ignored binary lines produces four aliases.

Clear the ignored positions to obtain a base, enumerate their combinations, then keep all decoded positions fixed. Two device selectors collide if their accepted address sets overlap; changing only an ignored bit cannot separate them.

blocks.title: Trace service using a stated priority policy
paragraphs: Assume requests H and L arrive together at time 0, H has higher priority, service is non-preemptive, H takes 3 microseconds, L takes 5, and there is no entry/exit overhead. H runs on [0,3); L runs on [3,8). L starts after 3 microseconds and finishes after 8.

If overhead, arrival time, masking or preemption differs, redraw the schedule. A priority rule alone does not determine total latency. Keep request time, service start, service duration and completion time separate.

blocks.title: Choose the mechanism for the stated workload
paragraphs: Compare the time spent repeatedly checking status with the cost of handling an interrupt and transferring the data. Frequent tiny events and rare events can favor different arrangements; quantify only the costs actually specified.

For an interrupt trace, list arrivals, enabled/masked requests and priority, apply the allowed preemption rule, then add all stated overhead. Never silently assume that every new request interrupts the current handler.

blocks.title: Make timing and decoding assumptions visible
paragraphs: Check selected drivers and handshakes, enumerate aliases from ignored bits, and construct interrupt timelines from explicit arrivals, priorities and overhead.
Practice separates deterministic address/timing checks from open bus-organization reasoning. The address workbench explores aliases without claiming a universal hardware decoder.

cards.prompt: Is high-impedance a third Boolean data value?
cards.answer: No. It means the output releases the line. Another selected driver or specified circuit behavior must establish valid bus data.

cards.prompt: How many aliases arise from k independently ignored address bits?
cards.answer: 2^k combinations share the same decoded bits, within the specified address width. Changing an ignored bit does not select a different decoded location.

cards.prompt: How can two partially decoded device addresses collide?
cards.answer: Their accepted address sets overlap. Compare the decoded constraints or enumerate aliases; different printed base addresses alone do not prove separation.

cards.prompt: What information is needed to trace interrupt service time?
cards.answer: Arrival times, priorities/masks, service durations, overhead and the permitted preemption policy. Priority alone is insufficient.

cards.prompt: Why is interrupt-driven I/O not automatically cheaper than polling?
cards.answer: Interrupt entry/exit and handler work also cost time. Compare actual event frequency and specified costs rather than assuming one mechanism always wins.

guided.title: Explain a valid shared-bus transfer
guided.prompt: Explain why selecting a device, releasing other data drivers and waiting for valid data are three distinct requirements.
rubric: Selection identifies the participant; driver control avoids contention; completion/timing establishes when data may be sampled.
High-impedance is release, not a valid third bit.
Use the stated synchronous or handshake contract; no unspecified timing diagram is reconstructed.
